rows.speaker: أبي العالية والمبرد
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya and al-Mubarrad say Israelites expelled people they had subdued, so the verse’s ransom refers to other people of their religion, not those expelled.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي العالية والمبرد، وقال: ليس الذين أخرجوهم الذين فودوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reads the phrase as taking ransom: Israelites fought one another, captured some, then collected ransom for prisoners.
rows.anchor: ولكن معناه تأخذ الفداء، يعني يقاتل بعضكم بعضا، فإذا أخذه أسيرا أخذ الفداء

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the prohibition concerns expulsion; partial belief and disbelief mean concealing and not practicing some scripture while accepting other parts.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مسلم، وهو محرم عليكم) يعني الإخراج محرم عليكم أفتؤمنون ببعض الكتاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and Ibn Jurayj say expelling fellow Israelites is disbelief while ransoming them is belief.
rows.anchor: فقيل: إخراجهم كفر، وفداؤهم إيمان، عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن جريج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says this conduct itself obliges them to disbelieve in part of scripture.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يلزمكم الكفر ببعض الكتاب بهذا الصنيع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says their covenant forbade killing, expulsion, and aiding against Israelites, but required ransoming captives; they obeyed only the ransom command, even ransoming someone they would later kill.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد: إن وجدته في يد غيرك فديته، ثم تقتله بيدك

rows.speaker: أبي القاسم
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim identifies the recompense as killing and expulsion, or alternatively the disbelief and belief they displayed.
rows.anchor: قيل: القتل والإخراج، وقيل: الكفر والإيمان الذي معهم، عن أبي القاسم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim includes killing, expulsion, and ransom among the acts whose recompense is asked about.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القتل والإخراج والفداء، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The worldly disgrace is explained either generally as humiliation or specifically through the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir and the killing and enslavement of Banu Qurayza’s families.
rows.anchor: يعني ذلا وصغارا، وقيل: إخراج بني النضير عن ديارهم، وقيل: قتل بني قريظة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The afterlife punishment is described as unbearable, hopeless punishment; other reports call it harsher than worldly punishment or harsher because it lasts.
rows.anchor: قيل: عذاب لا روح فيه مع اليأس في التخلص، وقيل: أشد من عذاب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the first account of the punishment as more apparent, more deterrent, and broader in benefit.
rows.anchor: والأول أظهر وأزجر وأعم في الفائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement threatens them: God knows their inward states and will requite them.
rows.anchor: تهديد لهم، بأنه عالم بسرائرهم، فيجازيهم على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two readings connect covenant-breaking to what precedes: the covenant verse introduces the breach, or breaking the covenant is itself a reason they disbelieved, as with the signs.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون على قوله: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم الآية. فلما ذكر الميثاق ذكر النقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns covenant-breaking as an act that can reach disbelief and says its recurrence among the Jews is signaled by “whenever”; most broke faith, though a few believed.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على قبح نقض العهد، وأن فيه ما يبلغ حد الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means casting or throwing aside; waraʾ is the opposite of what is in front, and the back is opposite the belly.
rows.anchor: النبذ: الطرح، نبذت الشيء نبذا فهو منبوذ. ووراء: نقيض قدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted reading has nominative muṣaddiq as an adjective of “Messenger”; Arabic also permits accusative, construing him as coming in confirmation.
rows.anchor: مصدق بالرفع، وهو القراءة، صفة للرسول، ويجوز في العربية النصب

rows.speaker: السدي وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and most exegetes identify the Messenger who came to the Jews of Muhammad’s time as Muhammad himself.
rows.anchor: قيل: محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن السدي وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim takes “Messenger” to mean the message, citing a poetic line about not having sent anyone as a messenger; ʿAli ibn ʿIsa calls this contrary to the apparent sense and rare in usage.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالرسول الرسالة، قال الشاعر: لقد كذب الواشون ما بحت عندهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “Confirming what they have” can mean that Muhammad matched earlier books’ prophecies or confirmed the Torah as truth from God.
rows.anchor: قيل: مصدق لكتبهم؛ لأنه جاء على الصفة التي تقدمت البشارة، وقيل: يصدق بالتوراة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies what they have as both the Torah and the Gospel.
rows.anchor: التوراة والإنجيل، عن الحسن، وقيل: التوراة؛ لأن الخبر عن اليهود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says it is the Torah alone, since the discussion concerns Jews rather than Christians.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التوراة؛ لأن الخبر عن اليهود دون النصارى

rows.speaker: أبي القاسم
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim says the phrase is repeated instead of a pronoun because it means the Jewish scholars, so the referent differs in meaning.
rows.anchor: الأول: أنه أريد به علماء اليهود، فأعيد ذكرهم لاختلاف المعنى، عن أبي القاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although they retained the Torah, they cast it aside by failing to act on it for the sake of leadership.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لما لم يعملوا بها ابتغاء للرئاسة صاروا نابذين لها وراء ظهورهم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says they read the Torah in front of them but cast aside acting on it.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: هو بين أيديهم يقرؤونه، ولكن نبذوا العمل به

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna says they wrapped and gilded the Torah but did not make its lawful rules lawful or its forbidden rules forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: أدرجوه في الحرير والديباج، وحلوه بالذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says rejecting the Messenger’s new Book also meant casting aside the earlier scripture that contained the prophecy about him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما جاءهم الرسول بهذا الكتاب، ولم يقبلوه صاروا نابذين للكتاب الأول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They seemed ignorant of the truth, though they knew it and disbelieved from envy and stubbornness.
rows.anchor: قيل: لا يعلمون أنه حق وصدق، والمراد أنهم علموا فكفروا بغيا وعنادا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations say they seemed unaware of the punishment their action entailed or treated themselves as ignorant of scripture’s contents.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كأنهم لا يعلمون ما عليهم في ذلك من العقاب. وقيل: كأنهم لا يعلمون ما في كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting God’s Book by deliberate refusal to act on it is disbelief; knowingly committing the sin makes it graver and its punishment greater.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن من لم يعمل بكتاب الله ردا وعنادا يكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each prophet has a scripture; people need not know a scripture whose practice is not required, though general faith in it is an obligation and a grace.
rows.anchor: به، ولا تكون معرفته لطفا لنا، وإن كان الإيمان بها في الجملة من تكليفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet may be sent without a book; prophetic scriptures nevertheless serve as proof because people refer to them to know and judge the truth.
rows.anchor: نعم، وتدل على أن كتب الأنبياء حجة لولا ذلك لم يقل: ليحكم بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief after clarification and removal of excuses merits warning, showing that the fault lies with the people themselves.
rows.anchor: لما كفروا بعد البيان وإزاحة العلة استحقوا الوعيد فيوجب أنهم أتوا من قبل أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reasoning refutes compulsion: if God does not hold people accountable without clarification, he cannot justly hold them accountable when he has made them unable or given them no path.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يؤاخذ متى لم يبين، فكيف يؤاخذ إذا لم يقدر، ولم يجعل له سبيلا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book judges disputes because some err through neglect and others through excess; it clarifies the truth, as the Qur’an does about Jewish and Christian disagreements over Jesus.
rows.anchor: بعضهم كفر بالتقصير، وبعضهم بالغلو، فبين الكتاب الحق في ذلك

words: فهدى الله الذين آمنوا لما اختلفوا فيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both sides of the disagreement are false, and divine guidance leads believers away from both.
rows.anchor: على أن كلا الاختلافين باطل، وأن الهدى في خلافهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets bring promise and warning before detailed law, since rational matters and monotheism are first taught, then the legal rules are explained.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم ذلك قبل الشرع؛ لأنه تقدم البشارة والإنذار في العقليات والتوحيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation treats the coming as the arrival of God’s signs, elevating their significance as one might say the king arrived when his great army came.
rows.anchor: تأتيهم دلائل آياته، فجعل مجيء الآيات مجيئا له على التفخيم لشأن الآيات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes it as the coming of God’s command; the command and the signs it brings about are equivalent here.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يأتيهم أمر الله، كقوله في موضع آخر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third reading treats “in” as “with,” making the sense that God’s punishment comes with clouds and angels.
rows.anchor: قيل: (في) بمعنى الباء وحروف الصفات يبدل بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan understands the canopies as a covering of cloud.
rows.anchor: في ظلل قيل: سترة من الغمام، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak understands the canopies as pieces of cloud.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قطع من السحاب، عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud heightens awe because tremendous signs arrive within it; alternatively, the terrors are likened to clouds.
rows.anchor: جلائل آياته تأتي في غمام فيكون أهول، وقيل: يأتي بأهوال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “The matter is settled” can mean that punishment becomes due or that judgment and resurrection’s affairs are finished.
rows.anchor: وقضي الأمر قيل: وجب العذاب، وقيل: فرغ من الحساب وأمور القيامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation says events have run their course according to their established pattern.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جرى أموره على سننه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: All affairs return to God because ownership of creation disappears at the gathering, making everything appear returned to its owner.
rows.anchor: كانت الأمور كلها له ملك عباده أشياء زالت جميعها في الحشر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God alone becomes judge and manager, like someone returning an affair to another to manage even if he did not originate it.
rows.anchor: يرجع إليه بأن يكون هو الحاكم والمدبر لا حكم لأحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading says all affairs return to God’s will, so neither disbelief nor disobedience occurs.
rows.anchor: يرجع الأمر إلى مراده، فلا يكون كفر ولا معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Affairs” includes worldly and afterlife matters; God reckons people’s deeds and recompenses them.
rows.anchor: الأمور: يعني أمور الدنيا والآخرة، فيحاسب عباده على أعمالهم، ثم يجازيهم عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and al-Suddi explain the deaf, mute, and blind as deaf to proof, unable to speak truth, and blind to evidence.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي، وهذا على التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description is a simile: by refusing to hear truth, speak it, or see its proofs, they act like people who lack those senses.
rows.anchor: وهذا على التشبيه يعني لما لم يسمعوا الحق، ولم يتكلموا به، ولم يبصروا الأدلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They may actually bear these qualities on the Day of Resurrection, as another verse says they are gathered blind, mute, and deaf.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنهم على هذه الصفة يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “They do not reason” means either that they do not know the truth or that they are as if without reason because they do not use it.
rows.anchor: فهم لا يعقلون قيل: لا يعلمون الحق، وقيل: هم بمنزلة من لا عقل له

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli argues that the verse refutes the epistemologists: if they necessarily knew the religion’s truth, they would not deserve this description.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: الآية تدل على بطلان قول أصحاب المعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who will not heed a preacher is like an animal that cannot reason.
rows.anchor: من لا يقبل قول الواعظ الداعي كأنه بمنزلة البهيمة التي لا تعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naʿaq is a shepherd’s cry to sheep, while the same verb describes a crow’s call.
rows.anchor: نعق الراعي بالغنم ينعق: إذا صاح بها، ونعق الغراب: إذا صوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling and supplication are similar, but a command is a superior’s request to an inferior whereas supplication is a request to someone higher.
rows.anchor: والدعاء: طلب الفعل من المدعو، ونظيره الأمر، والفرق بينهما يظهر بالرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deafness, muteness, and blindness are impairments that block perception through those senses.
rows.anchor: والصمم والبكم والعمى آفات تمنع الإدراك بهذه الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣumm is nominative as a new clause, “they are deaf”; al-Farraʾ also permits an accusative reading as censure.
rows.anchor: صم رفع على الاستئناف، أي هم صم، وأجاز الفراء النصب في العربية على الذم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta reports that the verse was revealed concerning the Jews.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء أنها نزلت في اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After noting that unbelievers were called to Islam but did not answer and clung to imitation, the passage introduces a parable about them.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الكفار وأنهم دعوا إلى الإسلام فلم يجيبوا، وركنوا إلى التقليد ضرب لهم مثلا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The opening “likeness” can mean either their description or their simile.
rows.anchor: ومثل الذين كفروا قيل: صفتهم، وقيل: شبههم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والربيع
rows.claim: The preferred reading compares unbelievers’ response to the Prophet’s call with animals that hear a caller’s noise but cannot understand it; the omitted object is inferred from context.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن في البيان، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والربيع

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: A second reading compares idolaters invoking their gods to calling animals that cannot understand, so worshipping an uncomprehending stone is even more blameworthy.
rows.anchor: بالذم والجهل، حكاه أبو القاسم وغيره

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd compares idol invocation to calling into a mountain and hearing only an echo: apparent response has no real benefit, as with idols.
rows.anchor: ليس لذلك حقيقة ولا فيه فائدة، عن أبي زيد

words: فإن طلقها فلا تحل له من بعد حتى تنكح زوجا غيره
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report attributes the occasion to ʿAʾisha; another names Tamima, wife of Rifaʿa al-Qurazi, who after a triple divorce married ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr and asked to return to her first cousin-husband.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآية في عائشة، وقيل: تميمة بنت عبد الرحمن القرظي، وكانت تحت رفاعة بن وهب

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In the report, the Prophet tells the woman she cannot return to Rifaʿa until she and her second husband have had intercourse; Abu Bakr is present, and “honey” is an eloquent euphemism for sex.
rows.anchor: وقال: أتريدين أن ترجعي إلى رفاعة؛ لا، حتى تذوقي من عسيلته، ويذوق من عسيلتك وأبو بكر جالس يسمع

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When she later says her second husband had intercourse, the Prophet calls her first statement a lie and says he cannot accept her later claim; after his death Abu Bakr refuses her return, and Umar threatens to stone her if she returns.
rows.anchor: فقال: كذبت قولك الأول، فلا نصدقك في الآخر، فلبثت حتى قبض رسول الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes “if he divorces her” as an explanation of “release with kindness,” on the view that release means divorce.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن قولة: فإن طلقها تفسير لقوله: أو تسريح بإحسان، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies this divorce as the third divorce.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هي التطليقة الثالثة، عن السدي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says the Qur’an establishes the marriage contract while the Sunna establishes intercourse as the condition for remarriage.
rows.anchor: قيل: العقد يعلم بالكتاب، والوطء بالسنة، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view finds both the contract and intercourse in the Qur’anic wording because “marriage” can denote both.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل كلاهما يعلم بالكتاب؛ لأن النكاح يعبر به عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says intercourse is implied by “marry” and the contract by “a husband,” an eloquent and concise euphemism.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: وهو من الكنايات الفصيحة، والإيجاز العجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the second husband divorces her, she and the first husband may remarry under a new contract, by agreement of the scholars.
rows.anchor: أي لا مأثم على المرأة والزوج الأول أن يتراجعا يعني بنكاح جديد باتفاق أهل العلم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim glosses “if they think” as knowing, being certain, or believing that they will uphold God’s limits.
rows.anchor: قيل: علما، وقيل: أيقنا، وقيل: اعتقدا، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Upholding God’s limits can mean knowing the marriage is not a deceptive arrangement or observing each spouse’s duties toward the other.
rows.anchor: قيل: علما أن نكاحهما على غير دلسة، وقيل: يعملان بما أمر الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s limits are his commands and prohibitions, which he makes clear to people who know and benefit from the signs.
rows.anchor: وتلك يعني ما نبينه حدود الله أوامره ونواهيه يبينها يفصلها

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says “people who know” means rational people, since they are the addressees; other views say the knowledgeable benefit from the signs or are singled out for distinction.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم العقلاء؛ لأنهم المخاطبون، عن أبي مسلم، وقيل: أراد به من يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel brought the Qur’an to Muhammad’s heart by causing him to recite it and retain it in memory.
rows.anchor: والمراد به يقرأ عليه فيحفظه كأنه نزله على قلبه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “By God’s permission” means either by God’s command or by his knowledge.
rows.anchor: قيل: بأمره نزل عليه، وقيل: بعلمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Confirmation may mean agreement with earlier books, their contents, their truth, or their teaching of monotheism and justice despite differences in law, or confirmation of Muhammad’s description.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يصدقه في التوحيد والعدل، وإن خالفه في الشرائع، وقيل: في صفة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What preceded the Qur’an here is the Torah.
rows.anchor: وما بين يديه هو التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is guidance, meaning direction and clarification; it is called guidance especially of believers because they follow it, though others could be guided by it.
rows.anchor: وهدى دلالة وبيانا، وخص المؤمنين به لاهتدائهم به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Guidance, mercy, reward, and glad tidings describe the good news of lasting bliss for believers, even if the revelation also brings punishment to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رحمة وثوابا وبشرى يعني إن كان نزل بالعذاب على الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Guidance and glad tidings” can describe the Qur’an, construed as what Gabriel sent down, or Gabriel, who brings guidance and good news.
rows.anchor: قلنا: فيه وجهان: الأول: القرآن كأنه قال: نزله هدى وبشرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second grammatical possibility makes Gabriel himself guidance and glad tidings, meaning that he brings them.
rows.anchor: الثاني: جبريل هدى وبشرى، أي يأتي بالهدى والبشرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that some Jews regarded Gabriel as an enemy; the Prophet’s accusation and their silence rather than denial demonstrate this.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن في اليهود من كان يعتقد عداوة جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address at the start is to husbands.
rows.anchor: وإذا طلقتم النساء خطاب للأزواج

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: “Reaching their term” means approaching the end of the waiting period, since a husband cannot retain a wife after it expires; Arabic also uses “reached” for nearing a place.
rows.anchor: معناه: قاربن وشارفن أجلهن، عن الحسن وغيره من أهل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting period is counted in menstrual cycles for menstruating women, months for those who do not menstruate, and childbirth for pregnant women.
rows.anchor: الأقراء في ذوات الحيض، والأشهر فيمن لا تحيض، والوضع فيمن بها حمل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and Mujahid say to retain them by taking them back before the waiting period ends.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد بمعروف أي بالقيام بما أمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو علي والأصم
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli and al-Asamm define honorable retention as fulfilling God’s duties toward her without intending harm; what reason or law recognizes as sound is maʿruf.
rows.anchor: عن أبي علي والأصم، والمعروف الذي يدعو إليه العقل أو الشرع للمعرفة بصحته

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says honorable retention requires witnesses to the return and does not permit return through intercourse alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بمعروف بإشهاد على الرجعة دون الرجعة بالوطء، عن ابن جرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To release them is to leave them until their waiting period expires, when they become their own decision-makers.
rows.anchor: أو سرحوهن أي طلقوهن بأن تتركوهن حتى تنقضي عدتهن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Harmful retention includes bad treatment or conduct, restricting maintenance during the waiting period, and prolonging the waiting period to transgress God’s limits.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التضييق في النفقة في العدة، وقيل: بتطويل العدة لتعتدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer deprives the wife of her right by violating God’s command and thereby deserves God’s threat.
rows.anchor: يعني بخس حقها حيث خالف أمر الله تعالى حتى استحق وعيد الله

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm and Abu Muslim explain this as forbidding people to treat God’s signs, commands, and obligations frivolously.
rows.anchor: عن الأصم وأبي مسلم. وقيل: آيات الله قوله:

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the signs in question as the rule “retention with kindness or release with good treatment.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: آيات الله قوله: (فإمساك بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان) عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The blessing includes the provision of spouses and wealth and the explanation of lawful and unlawful things.
rows.anchor: قيل: فيما أباح من الأزواج والأموال، وما بين من الحلال والحرام، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says the blessing is what God taught them when they were ignorant, or the blessing of faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بما علمكم وكنتم جهالا، عن الأصم. وقيل: بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God sent down is the Book and wisdom, including the knowledge and legal rules it conveys; it admonishes them to stop disobeying.
rows.anchor: وهو الكتاب والحكمة يعني العلوم التي دل عليها، والشرائع التي بينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God means avoiding sins that lead to punishment, or avoiding the punishment by avoiding sins; God knows all their actions.
rows.anchor: أي اتقوا معاصيه المؤدية إلى عقابه، وقيل: اتقوا عذابه باتقاء معاصيه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Jews of Muhammad’s time addressed him, then the passage returned to their forebears’ account of the calf.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم اليهود الذين كانوا في عصر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قالوا ذلك له، ثم رجع إلى حديث أوائلهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli identifies them as the Jews in Moses’ time who said “we hear and disobey”; the author calls this the better reading because it explains the discourse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي علي، وهو الوجه؛ لأنه تبيين الكلام

rows.speaker: قتادة وأكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Qatada and most scholars explain that the calf’s love was made to enter their hearts.
rows.anchor: قيل: حب العجل، عن قتادة وأكثر أهل العلم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that Moses ground and burned the calf, scattered it into the sea, then told the people to drink; those who loved it showed gold on their lips, with a similar report from Ibn Jurayj.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: لما رجع موسى إلى قومه أخذ العجل وحرقه بالمبرد، ثم ذراه في اليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the meaning “love of the calf”: the verse mentions hearts, one does not say someone drank when only the lips were wetted, and this reading is clearer and held by most scholars.
rows.anchor: والأول الوجه لذكره القلوب، ولأنه لا يقال: أشرب من سقى الشفة، ولأنه أظهر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “Made to drink” can mean that love was put into their hearts, like a color being absorbed through close contact.
rows.anchor: قيل: أدخل قلوبهم حبه، كإشراب اللون لشدة الملازمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation uses watering as a metaphor: because they persisted in worshipping the calf, they are said to have been made to drink it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما داموا على عبادة العجل قيل: أشربوا لأن الشرب مادة الزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive does not require an outside agent: their intense attachment and habitual worship made the calf’s love settle in their hearts.
rows.anchor: لم يرد أن غيرهم فعل ذلك بهم، ولكن لفرط ولوعهم به، وإلفهم لعبادته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, those who adorned and invited them to calf worship—such as the Samiri, Iblis, and human and jinn devils—made them love it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أشركه من زينه عندهم ودعا إليه، كالسامري وإبليس وشياطين الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects saying God caused their calf-love: that would invalidate the rebuke, attribute forbidden adornment of idolatry to God, and imply he could send a messenger to call people to it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقال: إن الله تعالى فعل ذلك؛ لأنه ذمهم بذلك ووبخهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disbelief includes anthropomorphism, ignorance of God, and permitting worship of other than God.
rows.anchor: بكفرهم يعني لاعتقادهم التشبيه وجهلهم بالله، وتجويزهم العبادة لغير الله

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة والشعبي وقتادة وأبي العالية
rows.claim: Hasan, ʿIkrima, al-Shaʿbi, Qatada, and Abu al-ʿAliya say the first wrath followed disbelief in Jesus and the next followed disbelief in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وعكرمة والشعبي وقتادة وأبي العالية

rows.speaker: عطاء وعبيد بن عمير وأبي علي
rows.claim: ʿAta, ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, and Abu ʿAli say the first wrath followed earlier claims about ʿUzayr, God’s hand, and distortion of scripture; the next followed rejection of Muhammad and his revelation.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء وعبيد بن عمير وأبي علي

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm and Abu Muslim read the doubled wrath as emphatic, because wrath remained upon them and repeatedly fell on them.
rows.anchor: عن الأصم وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the first wrath was for worshipping the calf and the second for concealing Muhammad’s description and denying his prophethood.
rows.anchor: الأول: لعبادتهم العجل، الثاني: كتمانهم صفة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humiliation is attributed to the punishment because punishment causes humiliation; this is figurative attribution.
rows.anchor: يعني يهينهم الله بالعذاب، فأضاف الإهانة إلى العذاب لأنه سبب له توسعا ومجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends the Prophet when he knows it serves people’s welfare, not from whim.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أنه تعالى يبعث النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من حيث يعلم أن المصلحة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns preferring worldly life over religion as a manifest loss.
rows.anchor: وتدل على ذم من آثر الدنيا على الدين، وأنه قد خسر خسرانا مبينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because sinners merit punishment and wrath for their own deeds, the verse establishes human agency and refutes determinists who say God creates people’s acts.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن العاصي يستحق العقاب والغضب بفعله، فتدل أن للعبد فعلا

rows.speaker: أبو الهذيل
rows.claim: Abu al-Hudhayl challenges Hafs al-Fard: after Hafs says he knows only God and God’s creation, Abu al-Hudhayl asks whether he is angry because God is God; Hafs says no, illustrating agency.
rows.anchor: وقد قال أبو الهذيل - رحمه الله - لحفص الفرد: هل تعلم غير الله وغير خلقه؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaliṣa means pure or exclusive, the opposite of mixed; the root conveys something cleared of every admixture.
rows.anchor: الخالصة والصافية من النظائر، ونقيضه: الشائب، يقال: خلص خلوصا

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة والنحو
rows.claim: Language and grammar scholars, including Abu ʿAli, define wishing as speech such as “I wish I had wealth”; Abu Hashim instead calls it an inward meaning, and the author prefers the speech account.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي علي، وقيل: هو معنى في القلب، عن أبي هاشم، والأول أصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle layta is the original expression of wishing, but an interrogative may replace it, as in the cited question asking whether intercessors will appear.
rows.anchor: و (ليت) أصل في أداة التمني، ثم يقام الاستفهام مقامه كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duna can describe lower location, lower rank, or exclusive possession; exclusivity is intended here.
rows.anchor: و (دون): يستعمل على ثلاثة أوجه: دونه في المكان، ودونه في الشرف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli defines death as an accident opposed to life, which the author calls the correct account; Abu Hashim describes it as life’s cessation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عرض يضاد الحياة، عن أبي علي وهو الصحيح

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبي العالية والربيع
rows.claim: Qatada, Abu al-ʿAliya, al-Rabiʿ, and most scholars say the challenge answered false Jewish claims that the Fire would touch them only briefly, only Jews or Christians enter Paradise, and they were God’s children and beloved.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة وأبي العالية والربيع، وأكثر أهل العلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the challenge came during their dispute with the Prophet: invoke death on whichever side was lying.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما جادلوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قيل: فتمنوا الموت

words: إن كانت لكم الدار الآخرة عند الله خالصة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to challenge them: if they are certain that Paradise and a good afterlife are reserved exclusively for them, they should wish for death if sincere.
rows.anchor: يعني خاصة، أي كنتم واثقين بخلوص الجنة لكم، وحسن حالكم في المعاد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “Apart from people” may particularly mean apart from God, Muhammad, and the Companions whom the Jews mocked and regarded as less entitled to truth, or it may be general in keeping with their claim that only Jews or Christians enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: قيل: من دون الله ومحمد، صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه - رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to ask for and desire death, as proof of their claim that the afterlife belongs to them.
rows.anchor: فتمنوا الموت أي سلوه وأريدوه إن كنتم صادقين فيما زعمتم وادعيتم
